issues.t: CVT hesitation, shudder or whine
issues.sym: The car hesitates or lunges when pulling away, jerks at low speed, whines, or feels like it is slipping. In bad cases the transmission stops changing ratio properly.
issues.why: The Mirage uses a continuously variable transmission (CVT). Owners report hesitation, shift shock, slipping and failures, and Mitsubishi issued bulletins to reprogram the CVT computer and update CVT service procedures.
issues.next: Have the CVT fluid level and condition checked and ask a dealer about software updates. Change the CVT fluid on schedule. A CVT that slips or whines loudly usually needs replacement, so check warranty coverage first.

issues.t: Front brakes wear out early or calipers stick
issues.sym: Grinding or squealing brakes, a burning smell, pulsing in the pedal, or pads and rotors needing replacement after only 10,000-30,000 miles.
issues.why: Premature front brake wear is the most-reported problem on the 2015 Mirage. Some owners found sticking or seized calipers that kept wearing out new pads and rotors.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected at every oil change. If pads wear out quickly, ask the shop to check that the calipers and slide pins move freely.

issues.t: Pulling, drifting and fast front tire wear
issues.sym: The car drifts or pulls to one side, the steering wheel sits off-center, or the front tires wear out early. Owners also notice it gets pushed around by crosswinds.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued repeated dealer notices on wheel alignment checks for Mirage pulling and drifting complaints. Light weight and narrow tires make it more sensitive to wind and road crown.
issues.next: Check tire pressures first, then get an alignment. If it still pulls, ask the dealer to follow Mitsubishi's alignment bulletin.

issues.t: Forward collision mitigation warning or not working
issues.sym: A forward collision or "system malfunction" warning comes on, or the automatic emergency braking does not warn or brake for cars or people ahead.
issues.why: Owners of 2021 and newer Mirages, which added forward collision mitigation, report the system faulting or not working, and dealers sometimes cannot find the cause.
issues.next: Keep the windshield area in front of the camera and the front sensor clean. Have the codes read by a dealer, and don't rely on the system until it is fixed.

issues.t: Airbags may be switched off by an SRS computer error (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light may come on, and the airbags might not deploy in a crash.
issues.why: Vibration from rough roads or a flat tire could make the airbag computer think its own sensor had failed, so it disabled the airbags. Dealers reprogram the computer (campaign 17V686).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get this done; it is free.

issues.t: Airbag impact sensor can delay deployment (recall)
issues.sym: The SRS airbag light may come on.
issues.why: High resistance in an airbag impact sensor on early 2014 Mirages could delay the front airbags or stop the side and curtain airbags. Dealers replace the sensors (campaign 15V594).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Wiring connector under driver carpet can corrode (recall)
issues.sym: Often no symptoms; an airbag light may come on. Wet carpet near the driver's left foot is a clue.
issues.why: Water and road salt can soak through the carpet and corrode a connector behind the kick panel, which could delay the front airbags. Dealers replace corroded connectors and add a waterproof sheet (campaign 15V815).
issues.next: Have the recall done, and dry out any wet carpet promptly.

issues.t: HID headlights can be mis-aimed (recall)
issues.sym: Poor night vision or other drivers flashing their lights at you.
issues.why: On 2017 Mirages with HID headlights, the horizontal aiming lock clips may not be secured, so the beams can be knocked out of aim. Dealers secure the clips (campaign 16V675).
issues.next: Check the recall status and have the headlight aim checked.

issues.t: Mirage G4 airbag warning light (recall)
issues.sym: The SRS airbag warning light comes on.
issues.why: Certain 2017-2018 Mirage G4 sedans built through November 2017 were recalled for a possible SRS warning lamp fault (campaign 19V330).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and schedule the free repair.

issues.t: Cold-start engine knocking noise (service campaign)
issues.sym: A knocking or rattling noise from the engine for a short time after a cold start.
issues.why: Mitsubishi ran a service campaign (SC-16-001) to reflash the engine computer for a cold-start engine noise; some engines were replaced, and replacement engines were back-ordered for a time.
issues.next: Ask a Mitsubishi dealer whether your car had the campaign done. If the noise continues, have it checked while the engine is cold.

issues.t: Stalling at low speed in hot weather
issues.sym: The engine stalls when slowing down or idling, mostly when it is hot outside.
issues.why: An overly rich air-fuel mixture could stall the engine. Mitsubishi released a bulletin to reprogram the engine computer and check a PCV hose that could come off (TSB-15-13-001).
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check for the engine computer update and inspect the PCV hose.

issues.t: Clutch wears out quickly (manual)
issues.sym: The clutch slips, the engine revs without the car speeding up, or the pedal feels different. Some owners needed a clutch around 20,000 miles.
issues.why: Clutch wear is reported early on manual-transmission Mirages, often in stop-and-go driving.
issues.next: Avoid riding the clutch and holding the car on hills with it. If it slips, replace it before it leaves you stranded.

issues.t: Automatic transmission harsh shifts or slipping
issues.sym: Hard or violent shifts, slipping, the transmission dropping into neutral, or gears failing, sometimes at highway speed.
issues.why: The automatic transmission is the most common complaint on the 1997-2002 Mirage. Owners report repeated failures.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips or shifts violently, avoid highway driving until it is diagnosed.

issues.t: Crankshaft pulley bolt can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: A wobbling pulley, squealing belts, and in the worst case the pulley falling off and loss of power steering.
issues.why: On Mirages with the 1.5L engine, the crankshaft pulley bolt could loosen. Dealers installed an improved bolt or retightened it (campaign 00V311).
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the recall was done. Any wobbling pulley needs attention right away.

issues.t: Crankshaft pulley bolt can loosen on 2000 models (recall)
issues.sym: A wobbling pulley, belt noise, and possible loss of power steering if the pulley comes off.
issues.why: The crankshaft pulley bolt on some 2000 Mirages could loosen. Dealers checked and retightened it and replaced damaged parts (campaign 01V340).
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the recall was done.

issues.t: Brake booster vacuum valve can stick (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels hard and the car takes more effort to stop.
issues.why: A badly made vacuum check valve in the hose to the brake booster could stick. Dealers replaced the hose (campaign 97V179).
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the recall was done. A hard brake pedal needs immediate attention.

issues.t: Stalling or no-start from a failed distributor
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, or it cuts out while driving and may not restart.
issues.why: RepairPal lists internal distributor faults as a common no-start cause on the older Mirage, and NHTSA complaints describe sudden stalling.
issues.next: Have the ignition system checked for spark. A failed distributor is usually replaced as a unit.

issues.t: Door hinges crack and doors sag
issues.sym: Doors creak, sag, drop when opened, or are hard to close; in bad cases the hinge breaks.
issues.why: Owners report door hinges cracking or collapsing. CarComplaints lists this on the 2001 Mirage, sometimes needing a new door.
issues.next: Lubricate the hinges and have sagging doors checked early, before the hinge or door mount cracks.

issues.t: Grinding brakes and warped rotors
issues.sym: Grinding or squealing when stopping, or a pulsing pedal and shaking steering wheel.
issues.why: Front pads and rotors wear and warp early on these cars, according to owner complaints and RepairPal.
issues.next: Have the pads and rotors measured and replace them together.

issues.t: Airbags not deploying in crashes
issues.sym: Owners report airbags that stayed closed in crashes, or in a few cases deployed without a crash.
issues.why: Airbag complaints are among the most common NHTSA reports for the 1997-2002 Mirage. Sensors and wiring age and can fail.
issues.next: If the airbag light is on, have the system scanned. Check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Rusted control arms and crossmember
issues.sym: Clunking from the front suspension, wandering steering, or rust holes in the control arms.
issues.why: In salt-belt states the front control arms and crossmember can rust through on these older cars.
issues.next: Have the suspension inspected for rust at every oil change or inspection. Rusted-through arms must be replaced.
